restrictions: Messages are exactly 64 bytes (one root block, flags 11, length 64, counter 0).
Grouped birthday: 2^96 groups; shared m0..m14; enumerate all m15.
K_full is the full 256-bit partial-eval digest. Briggs-Torczon sparse set indexes by top 140 bits, stores K_full, never clears sparse[]; membership via dense[sparse[idx]]==idx and sparse[idx]<n.
Unequal-K index hits discard with Word ops only (no target compression). Equal K_full triggers two reference compressions; V_max=8.
Per-message Word ops = 297 = 252 inner + 14 pack + 28 BT/K-compare + 3 loop. T_ver<=16. No expectations in T.
Declared score-critical cost heuristic H-COST-BT-SPARSE for the 28-op BT envelope (replaces unsupported implicit H-COST-SPARSE-21 from c36797d2).
F2 is selected-pair displacement (Pr<=2^-12), not run-wide unequal-K hit probability.
Repair of c367 not_evaluable; retains c145/4dd cost repairs. Unkeyed BLAKE3-256; 2 rounds.

heuristics.statement: For uniformly random independent group prefixes and exhaustive m15 enumeration, the 2^128 digests behave like independent uniform 256-bit strings for bounding F1, selected-pair F2, and F4, up to a negligible additive gap covered by the allowance between the model bound (>0.3932) and claimed success probability 0.39.
heuristics.scope: Success-probability claim only. Does not justify expectation-for-worst-case substitutions in the time bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer matched-scale digest-xor-mask experiments at widths 16, 20, and 24 with N_t^2/2^w=1, plus single-group stress, extrapolated to full 256-bit collision statistics under H1.
heuristics.limitations: H1 unproved. Truncation cannot detect almost-permutations. No full-scale collision known.

heuristics.statement: On the classical 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5, the Briggs-Torczon procedure in proof §2.1 implements membership test, insert, and unequal-K discard for a top-140-bit index with never-cleared sparse[] in at most 28 charged primitive word operations per message, including one 256-bit K_full compare and address arithmetic margin.
heuristics.scope: Only the 28-op BT envelope inside the 297-ops/msg candidate ledger for this algorithm. Does not cover partial-eval inner body (separately counted) or reference compressions (T_ver).
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard Briggs-Torczon correctness (dense[sparse[i]]==i filter) is extrapolated from the classical data-structure argument to word-addressable sparse[0..2^140) without an initialization pass. No experiment measures RAM op counts; the bound is analytic from the op list.
heuristics.limitations: Not empirically microbenchmarked. If word-addressing a 2^140 sparse table were deemed to require multi-op page walks beyond the 28-op margin, the ledger would need a higher BT charge (possibly losing the undercut of ~127.481).
